shots.desc: Split screen: left ordinary kid struggling at piano while calendar flips DAY 1→10; right Eli at piano with clock advancing 1 hour. Labels 10 HOURS / 1 HOUR.
Top-down piano keys lighting up in a fluent melody (match-cut source).
Match cut: piano keys become a laptop keyboard; code typing.
Keyboard becomes a textbook page; a "1 DAY = 10 DAYS" counter; pencil annotating.
Page folds into a football tactics board; arrows draw a play.
School exterior at dusk; title card WHAT IF YOU COULD LEARN ANYTHING 10x FASTER? glows in.
Heroic low-angle: Eli in hallway, blinding backlight, rays, camera spins in like a superhero reveal.
Flat awkward classroom wide: teacher at ENGLISH board points at Eli: "Eli. The answer?"
Eli medium shot, confidently wrong: "Uh... thirty-seven?"
Extreme close-up on the teacher's unamused eyes behind glasses: "We're in English class." Board reads ENGLISH behind.
Class laughs (extras with happy faces bobbing); Eli sinks in his chair.
Close-up Eli, deflated, slumped face on desk.
Football field: Eli swings to kick, misses the ball entirely, falls on his back. Ball rolls away.
Side-profile piano: the rolling ball becomes the stool wheel; Eli plays awful notes, keys flash red.
Overhead: sheet music flutters down and becomes a math test with a huge red F.
Outside school at dusk: Eli on a bench; Noah (yellow cap, blue shirt) slides into frame holding his own D- test.
Noah close-up, deadpan: "Dude, we're so cooked."
Eli reverse close-up, flat: "You think?"
Dawn establishing: Eli's window at sunrise, alarm clock reads 6:00 AM.
Over-the-shoulder at desk: Eli rubs his eyes over messy notes; DAY 7 on the wall calendar (a week of struggle).
Notebook insert: messy crossed-out working, a red question mark.
Extreme close-up pencil: the messy steps rearrange themselves into a clean, ordered sequence (pattern recognised).
Close-up: Eli's eyes widen, lamp-lit.
Overhead page: problem after problem gets a green tick, tick, tick.
Proof graphic over a dimmed desk: big timer 00:00→06:00 while ordinary-Eli bar fills to 60 min; comparison "BEFORE 60 MIN / NOW 6 MIN".
Beat of silence, then Eli close-up: "Wait... what?"
Overhead: Eli's old F math test; red crosses flip to green ticks one by one; grade becomes 9/10.
The rule card (objection handling): "LEARNS 10× FASTER FROM PRACTICE" with crossed-out myths: instant knowledge, super strength, perfect judgment.
Bedroom: Eli stands up from the desk with a determined grin, cracks knuckles.
Music room wide at sunset: upright piano waiting; label FIRST: PIANO.
Eli at the piano, confident: "Okay. How hard can this be?"
Overhead hands: wrong keys flash red, discordant notes.
Eli wincing close-up as the narrator deadpans "Pretty hard, apparently."
Time-lapse: sunlight slides across the room, clock spins one hour, Eli practising; PRACTICE 0:00→1:00 bar fills; finger positions corrected.
Slow lateral dolly along the keyboard: correct keys glow gold and release musical-note shapes that float in rhythm.
Field at sunset: Eli tries to trap the ball; it bounces off his shin and rolls away. Frustrated.
Extreme low angle beside the ball: Eli's foot taps it repeatedly; dotted trajectory lines get tighter and tidier with each rep; rep counter.
Wide: a clean skill move — Eli flicks the ball up, volleys it into the goal net (net ripples).
Noah arrives at the touchline, jaw on the floor: "Bro, since WHEN could you do that?!"
Eli juggling, shrugging, equally amazed: "I don't know!"
Flashcard HOLA flips to こんにちは, flips again; practice timeline at the bottom keeps filling.
The last flashcard slides and becomes a laptop screen: code types, an ERROR appears, gets fixed, BUILD OK.
The coded animation (a little bouncing gold ball) hops out of the screen into the real bedroom; Eli watches it, delighted.
Limits #1: Eli asleep on his textbook at 2:00 AM, lamp still on — he still needs sleep.
Limits #2: on the field Eli does a perfect trick, then a bigger kid simply out-sprints him to the ball. Labels SKILL ✓ / STRENGTH & SPEED ✗.
SAME classroom angle as S008 (deliberate repeat). MATH on the board now; teacher asks; Eli raises his hand and answers.
Match cut: the old F test is swept aside by a new test stamped A+.
Teacher close-up: glasses slide down in genuine surprise.
Students crowd around Eli's desk holding out notebooks and questions.
Hallway: friends point at things — a guitar, a basketball hoop poster, a chess club flyer; Eli nods to each, hungry to learn.
A cocky student (green cap) slaps a scrambled Rubik's cube on Eli's desk: "Bet you can't solve this."
Eli close-up, sly confident smile: "Give me ten minutes."
Obsession montage A: Eli centred, front-on; puzzle cube then chessboard swap in front; friends behind him gradually walk away; light shifts from warm to cool.
Obsession montage B: same framing; a book then a circuit diagram; background now empty; cool blue light.
Robotics workshop, warm afternoon: Eli and Noah build the robot together and high-five. Two benches: Eli's (left) and Noah's (right, blue tool tray).
Robot close-up: red stripe (Eli) and blue stripe (Noah) side by side — built together.
A poster on the wall: ROBOTICS CUP — WINNER QUALIFIES FOR STATE. Calendar crosses off months.
Split pace: Eli works at blurring speed (motion-trail hands, code scrolling), Noah slowly reads a manual.
Noah eagerly points at his sensor drawing: "the metal barriers could confuse this sensor. I added a backup on the left..."
Insert of Noah's diagram: METAL barrier note, BACKUP sensor labelled LEFT; cut to the real robot's blue backup box on its left side.
Eli grabs the component without looking up: "Already fixed it." Noah's sentence is cut off.
Over Eli's shoulder: Noah tries again, "Oh. Well, what about the steering?"
Eli, back half-turned, still typing: "Fixed that too."
Noah close-up, hurt: "Dude, can I at least do something?"
Eli, not looking up: "I mean... I'll probably finish it faster."
HOLD on Noah (medium close-up) in silence; the upbeat music is gone; he slowly lowers his blue screwdriver to the bench — a small isolated click.
Wide: Noah walks out of the workshop door without a word; Eli keeps working. Noah's workstation is left empty (tray + stool, no Noah).

One fixed wide over several afternoons: sunlight sweeps across the workshop again and again; Eli alone works faster, the robot grows more polished; Noah's bench stays empty. The photo of the two friends sits on Eli's bench (planted).
Close-up: Eli glances at the empty stool, then back to work. Cool light.
Tournament hall wide: ROBOTICS CUP banner, floodlights, crowd in bleachers, course table with metal barriers.
Eli alone at the team station; the name card reads TEAM: ELI & NOAH (Noah is still officially registered). Telephoto glimpse: Noah, arms crossed, in the crowd.
Low tracking shot beside the robot as it races along the table, smooth and fast.
Overhead course: ROUND 1 — robot weaves around the barriers along the dotted route and finishes. ✓
Announcer with headset mic, arm raised: "And Eli's team advances to the final!" Crowd cheers.
Scoreboard flips to FINAL, clock 1:00 in red; music tightens.
Robot POV rushing toward a shiny METAL barrier; the orange main-sensor LED flickers.
Overhead: the robot suddenly veers the wrong way and bumps the barrier; red wrong-route line.
Eli panics, hands on head: "No, no, no. WHAT?!"
Diagnostic laptop: SOFTWARE ✓ OK, MOTORS ✓ OK — nothing wrong found; timer keeps falling.
Eli frozen at the station, the crowd blurred and muffled; the timer ticks.
Extreme close-up on Eli's eyes: no answer to learn from.
Eli looks up; telephoto isolates Noah (yellow cap) in the crowd.
Eli shouts across the hall: "NOAH!"
Noah stands up in the crowd: "What?!"
Eli, urgent: "Remember that sensor setup...? Why did you want to change it?"
Noah, frustrated: "Because the metal barriers mess with the readings! I told you that three weeks ago!"
Sepia flashback that matches S059/S060: Noah pointing at the diagram (BACKUP · LEFT); the soft tool-click returns.
Back in the hall: Eli freezes, guilty realisation.
Eli, desperate: "Okay! What do I do?!"
Noah points hard to his left: "Switch to the backup sensor! LEFT SIDE!"
Tight on the controller: Eli's thumb flips the switch MAIN → BACKUP SENSOR; zap.
Overlay: the main sensor's reading near metal is a jagged, distorted line; the backup reading is clean.
Low tracking: the blue backup LED lights up; the robot turns cleanly and slips past the barrier.
Overhead: robot recovers along the route to the finish; timer 0:03→0:01.
Extreme close-up on the checkered finish line: the robot's front wheel crosses it; FINISH horn, flash.
Crowd erupts, confetti; scoreboard WINNER.
Trophy held up in the foreground; Eli's eyeline passes the trophy toward Noah (rack focus from trophy to Eli).
Eli walks away from the trophy, threading through the cheering crowd toward Noah.
Two-shot by the bleachers, applause softening: Eli, sincere: "Dude... I'm sorry." Noah: "For what?"
Eli close-up: "Thinking I didn't need you."
Noah close-up, a teasing smile breaking through: "Yeah, that was pretty stupid."
Two-shot: Eli laughs "You're telling me." — Noah bumps his shoulder; they're friends again.
Dusk outside the school: the two friends walk home together carrying the robot and the trophy.
The robot's red and blue stripes side by side in warm light; the friends' photo propped next to it.
Match cut to the opening piano (overhead keys): Noah hits a terrible note.
Music room: Noah at the piano: "So... you gonna teach me that piano song or what?" Eli sits down beside him: "Yeah."
Noah, cheerfully: "Cool. It'll only take me ten hours."
Callback: Eli turns to camera with the same bewildered look from "Wait... what?": "...Oh my God." Comedic sting, cut to black with title.
